blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: User comments are stored in a database and later shown on an HTML page. Following the page, where should the HTML entity encoding happen?

options.text: When the comment is written out, encoded for the page's context
options.says: XSS prevention needs output encoding: data is encoded for the context it is rendered in (HTML, JavaScript, URL).

options.text: When the comment is saved, so that pages read text already encoded
options.says: The page asks for output encoding for the rendering context; a store-time encoding cannot know every context the text will appear in.

options.text: In the validation step, which refuses comments that hold HTML markup
options.says: The page makes output encoding the requirement for XSS prevention; validating input does not replace it.

questions.stem: A developer writes a query as a Java text block and fills in the user's search term with formatted(). What does the page say about this?

options.text: The text block quotes the inserted value, so the query is protected
options.says: A text block is only a string literal; the page says to still use PreparedStatement for parameterization.

options.text: The text block avoids escape bugs, but the term must still be a parameter
options.says: The page recommends text blocks to reduce escape-character bugs and says to still use PreparedStatement for parameterization.

options.text: The text block is safe as long as formatted() is given a %s placeholder
options.says: formatted() pastes the value into the SQL text; the page says to still use PreparedStatement for parameterization.

concepts: Encoding belongs to output, for the context the data is rendered in, not to input on its way into storage.
Writing SQL as a text block avoids escape bugs but values must still be bound as PreparedStatement parameters.
